q: 1. The weight and fall used in standard penetrometer test to drive the cone are .......
explain: The Standard Penetration Test (SPT) uses a standard weight of 65 kg (often cited as 63.5 kg in some codes) falling from a height of 75 cm.

q: 2. The soil investigation method using the penetrometers belongs to the category of .......
explain: Penetrometer tests (like SPT or CPT) are classified as sub-surface soundings because they measure the resistance of soil to the penetration of a sampler or cone.

q: 3. The failure of foundation of a building is due to
options: lateral escape of the supporting material
explain: Foundation failure can occur physically (lateral escape of soil), chemically/environmentally (moisture changes causing shrinkage), or structurally (uneven settlement leading to cracks).

q: 4. The number of blows recorded in a standard penetration test is for a penetration of .......
explain: The 'N' value in an SPT test is the number of blows required to drive the sampler for the last 30 cm of a 45 cm total penetration.

q: 5. The safe bearing capacity of the soil can be improved by ...........
options: draining the soil if water table is very near the base of the footing
explain: Bearing capacity can be increased by reaching stiffer strata (depth), filling voids (grouting), or removing pore water pressure (drainage).

q: 6. The bearing capacity of soils can be improved by
options: ramming the granular material like crushed stone in the soil
explain: Soil strength improves with depth (confinement), reduction of pore water pressure (drainage), and densification through the addition/compaction of granular materials.

q: 7. In a static penetrometer test the angle of the penetrating cone is ..........
explain: The standard cone used in static (Dutch) cone penetration tests has a base area of 10 cm² and an apex angle of 60°.

q: 8. The raft foundations are generally used when the required area of footing is ........ the total area of the structure.
explain: If individual footings would cover more than 50% (one-half) of the building area, a continuous raft (mat) foundation becomes more economical and effective at reducing differential settlement.

q: 9. In the case of soil investigation by boring, the record of soil samples arranged according the depth where they are found is known as .........
explain: A bore-log is a technical record that provides a detailed description of the soil layers encountered at various depths during a boring operation.

q: 10. The method of protecting the foundations in loose soils from caving in, is called
explain: Both timbering (planking and strutting) and shoring are used to provide temporary support to the sides of excavations in unstable soil.

q: 11. Well foundation is also known as .........
explain: A well foundation is a type of deep foundation, often used for bridges, which is technically referred to as a caisson.

q: 12. A pile which has an enlarged shape at the base is called .......
explain: A Franki pile (or pressure-injected foot pile) is characterized by a bulbous, enlarged base that provides high end-bearing resistance.

q: 13. A cast-in-situ concrete pile with one or more enlarged bulbs on its stem is called .........
explain: Under-reamed piles are bored cast-in-situ piles with one or more bulbs (reams) to provide better anchorage, especially in expansive soils like black cotton soil.

q: 14. Uniform distribution of loads from walls on piles is achieved by connecting the group of piles supporting the structure ...........
options: by tie rods at the bottom of the piles
by tie rods at the top of the piles
isolating the piles without any connection
explain: A pile cap (often in the form of a reinforced concrete beam) is used to tie the piles together and distribute the wall load evenly among them.

q: 15. The offsets in the stepped strip footing in brick masonry is ..........
explain: In standard brick masonry footings, the horizontal offset for each step is typically half a brick length (approx. 5 cm to 10 cm, with 5 cm being the minimum for stability).

q: 16. To improve the bearing capacity of the foundation, the cement grouting may be used if the foundation consists of .........
explain: Cement grouting is effective in rocks or coarse gravels where the grout can flow into fissures and voids to create a monolithic, stronger mass.

q: 17. If the soil is water logged, its bearing capacity may be improved by .........
explain: Water logging increases pore water pressure and reduces effective stress; removing the water through drainage significantly restores soil strength.

q: 18. The pile used to resist large horizontal or inclined force is ...........
explain: Batten (or Batter) piles are driven at an angle (inclined) to resist lateral forces from wind, water, or earth pressure.

q: 19. Width of wall footing (according to thumb's rule) is
explain: A common rule of thumb for footing width is twice the wall thickness plus 30 cm (2t + 300mm) to ensure proper load distribution to the soil.

q: 20. Which type of foundation is likely to be adopted for a 3 storey RCC framed building?
explain: For a standard 3-story framed building with good soil, isolated footings under each column are the most common and economical choice.

q: 21. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on sand is usually limited to
explain: Settlement in sand occurs more rapidly and is typically capped at 40-65 mm for raft foundations.

q: 22. The maximum differential settlement in case of foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: To prevent structural damage in clay, differential settlement (difference in settlement between two points) is limited to 40 mm.

q: 23. The maximum differential settlement, in case of foundation on sandy soils is usually limited to
explain: In sandy soils, the allowable differential settlement is stricter, usually limited to 25 mm.

q: 24. The maximum total settlement for isolated foundation on clayey soils should be limited to
explain: Isolated footings on clay are typically permitted a total settlement of up to 65 mm.

q: 25. While calculating the dead load of a building, the weight of brick masonry is taken as
explain: The unit weight of common brick masonry is standardly taken as 19.2 kN/m³ (approx 1920 Kg/m³).

q: 26. Lift becomes essential in building when the number of floors exceeds ..........
explain: In standard building bylaws, a lift is generally required when a building is G+3 (4 floors) or higher to ensure accessibility.

q: 27. Codes used in Nepal for building construction/ design is
explain: Nepal follows its own National Building Code (NBC) for structural design and safety.

q: 28. The piles driven to increase the capacity of supporting loads on vertical piles are known as ........
explain: Raking piles are driven at an angle (inclined) to the vertical to resist horizontal thrust or increase lateral stability.

q: 29. The size of the plate used in plate loading test in gravelly or sandy soils is ..........
explain: For non-cohesive (sandy or gravelly) soils, a standard smaller plate of 30 cm x 30 cm is often utilized.

q: 30. The angle of repose for dry sand may be taken as ..........
explain: The angle of repose (internal friction) for dry, loose sand is typically around 30 degrees.

q: 31. The lowest part of a structure which transmits the load to the soil is known as ..........
explain: The foundation is the sub-structure that transfers the building weight to the underlying soil or rock.

q: 32. The foundation in a building is provided to ..........
options: distribute the load over a large area
increase overall stability of the structure
transmit load to the bearing surface(sub soil) at a uniform rate
explain: Foundations ensure stability, prevent unequal settlement, and distribute heavy loads over a wider area to avoid soil failure.

q: 33. In masonry construction, excessive tension is not permissible and hence in order that the supporting area is fully in compression, the width of footing is so adopted that the centre of gravity of the load falls ..........
options: within the middle third of base
within the middle fifth of base
explain: To avoid tension at the base of a masonry footing, the eccentricity of the load must be limited so the resultant force stays within the middle third.

q: 34. The raft foundations are generally used when the required area of footing is ........ the total area of the surface.
explain: Standard practice dictates that if the total area of individual footings exceeds 50% (one-half) of the building area, a raft is used.

q: 35. A black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because it ..........
options: undergoes volumetric changes with the change of atmospheric conditions
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite clay which expands and contracts violently with moisture changes, causing structures to crack.

q: 36. A combined footing is commonly used ..........
options: when two columns are spaced close to each other
when two columns are spaced far apart
explain: When columns are so close that their individual footings would overlap, they are merged into a single combined footing.

q: 37. In combined footing ..........
options: center of gravity of the column loads must coincide with the center of gravity of the footing
explain: For uniform pressure distribution in a combined footing, the geometric center (C.G.) of the footing must coincide with the resultant C.G. of the loads from both columns.

q: 38. Batter piles are ..........
options: used to function as retaining walls
used to protect concrete deck or other water front structures from the abrasion or impact
driven at an inclination to resist large horizontal inclined forces
driven in granular soil with the aim of increasing the bearing capacity of the soil
explain: Batter piles (or raking piles) are driven at an angle to the vertical to resist lateral loads, such as wind or water pressure.

q: 39. The diameter of the drilled piles should not exceed ..........
explain: Standard drilled or bored piles for smaller structures typically range up to 600 mm in diameter.

q: 40. In order that the wall may be stable, the lowermost course of the wall footing is made ........ the width of the wall.
explain: According to the rule of thumb for spread footings, the width of the base of the foundation should be twice the width of the wall.

q: 41. The arrangement of supports provided underneath the existing structure without disturbing its stability, is known as ..........
explain: Underpinning is the process of strengthening or deepening the foundation of an existing structure.

q: 42. The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath, is known as ...........
explain: Underpinning is the process of strengthening or deepening the foundation of an existing building or structure.
